use_case_name: Transfer a Winning Order to Another Customer

claims.content: At main_flow step 3 (System verifies the 2nd-place finisher's eligibility and sends the 2nd-Chance transfer offer email), if there is no 2nd-place finisher to receive the offer, the 2nd-Chance email is not sent.

At main_flow step 3 (System verifies the 2nd-place finisher's eligibility and sends the 2nd-Chance transfer offer email), if the 2nd-Chance recipient has two accounts and is essentially bidding against themselves, or if a match is found on any of Customer Name, Customer Phone Number, Customer Email Address, Customer Member ID, or Customer Billing and/or Shipping Addresses between the 2nd-Chance recipient and the Winner, the 2nd-Chance email is not sent.

At main_flow step 3 (System verifies the 2nd-place finisher's eligibility and sends the 2nd-Chance transfer offer email), if the 2nd-place finisher's bid is below the item's unit cost, the 2nd-Chance email is not sent.

At main_flow step 3, after the 2nd-Chance email is sent, if the 2nd-Chance recipient does not respond to the email within 72 hours after it is sent, the item is returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

The system detects that the original winner's order has been cancelled due to non-payment within 7 days (168 hours) and that the item is in 'hold' status.
The system identifies the second-place finisher as the recipient of the 2nd-Chance transfer offer.

The system sends the 2nd-Chance transfer offer email to the second-place finisher, offering the item at their last bid price and presenting the Credit Card, PayPal or Amazon Payments, and Decline options.

If the Customer accepts the offer within three days by clicking the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button, the system generates the order and loads the Sign-In page; after signing in, the Customer is taken to the Returning Winners Payments Page to complete payment.
The Customer accepts the offer by clicking the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button.
Following acceptance, the system removes the item from 'hold' status, automatically generates an order, and ships it to the Customer; no further action by the Customer is needed.

The use case is triggered when a winning order is cancelled because the winning auction participant, who has PayPal or Amazon Payments set as their default Method of Payment, fails to pay within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, and the item is placed into 'hold' status.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer (second-place finisher) accepts a 2nd-Chance Offer to purchase the item at their last bid price after the original winner's order is cancelled.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The original winner's order is cancelled for non-payment and the item is placed on hold; the system sends a 2nd-Chance Offer email to the second-place finisher, and the Customer accepts the offer, completing the transfer of the winning order to that Customer at their last bid price.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The use case starts when the original winner's order has been cancelled for non-payment and the item is available via 2nd-Chance Offer to the second-place finisher.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has been offered and accepts the 2nd-Chance Offer, so the cancelled winning order is transferred to them at their last bid price.

claims.content: Diverges from Step 4: instead of clicking 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card', the Customer clicks the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button; the system generates the order and loads the Sign-In page, after which the Customer is taken to the Returning Winners Payments Page to complete payment.

Diverges from Step 4: when the Customer accepts via PayPal or Amazon Payments (including when that is their default Method of Payment), the system does not auto-process payment; instead it sends an email instructing the Customer to sign into their JTV account and complete payment within 7 days, after which the item is shipped.

Diverges from Step 4: after accepting via PayPal/Amazon Payments, the Customer selects 'Checkout Later' instead of paying immediately; the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a confirmation that the Customer can return to pay within 7 days (168 hours). Within that confirmation, the system provides a 'Return to Payments' link that closes the overlay and re-enables page links, and a 'JTVauctions Homepage' link that navigates the Customer away from the payment page.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The main flow serializes the PayPal/Amazon acceptance path (step 4) and the credit-card acceptance path (step 5) as consecutive steps, then applies step 6's 'following acceptance... ships... no further action' generically. This is contradictory: a Customer who accepts via PayPal/Amazon is sent to the Returning Winners Payments Page to complete payment, while step 6 claims no further action/shipment. Because these are mutually exclusive payment branches, the flow cannot lead cleanly to the unconditional postcondition that the item is removed from hold and to the conditional postconditions 3/4 on both branches.

[goal_mainflow_alignment] Main flow step 6 states that after acceptance the system ships the item to the Customer, but the goal slot's scope_contract explicitly lists 'Subsequent payment processing and shipping' under excluded_adjacent_actions. This makes the complete main flow behavior inconsistent with the goal's stated boundary.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger and the rest of the transfer flow assume that a second-place finisher exists to receive the 2nd-Chance Offer, but Preconditions only cover the original winner's cancellation, the item hold status, and the original winner's default payment method. Without an eligible second-place finisher, the transfer use case cannot be initiated even if all listed Trigger conditions occur.

The Main Flow only supports acceptance through the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button and then removes hold/generates order/ships. It does not contain a path where the Customer accepts via PayPal or Amazon Payments, so the postcondition stating that the Sign-In page is loaded for PayPal/Amazon acceptance is unreachable from the Main Flow.

Main Flow step 4 only models acceptance via the 'On File credit card' button. Despite step 3 offering PayPal/Amazon Payments as acceptance options, no main-flow step or branch follows those options to the Sign-In / Returning Winners Payments Page described in Postcondition 4. Therefore the PayPal/Amazon acceptance postcondition is not reachable from the supplied main flow.
